<reason>A won a competitive debate by making the choice easier: the dial is never empty, the motion is a capability not a mandate, and CON’s architecture/abuse/obligation harms stayed more conjectural than the nightly engagement default. B landed real damage on platform definition of “recommendation,” the primary-device lock, and the workaround tension, but never neutralized A’s comparison and lost execution when Rebuttal 1 was clipped.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Rebuttal 1 contradiction—CON treating the OS layer as both an unpickable cage and something teens shrug off with a spare phone—plus the “dial is never empty” pressure, which forced B onto a messier “deny the forced choice” line.</best_rebuttal>
